# Repository-specific harden-runner egress allow-list (supplemental).
#
# This file is the "supplemental" half of the block-mode allow-list.
# The baseline is the shared Linux Foundation RelEng list at
# lfreleng-actions/.github, pinned to a commit in each workflow that
# consumes it; lfreleng-actions/harden-runner-block-action fetches
# both, merges them (baseline first, duplicates removed, first-seen
# order kept) and exports the result as CONNECTION_ALLOW_LIST for a
# following step-security/harden-runner step in 'block' mode.
#
# How workflows reference this file
# ---------------------------------
# Workflows name it as 'tykeal/homeassistant-guesty//' -- a search
# chain rather than an explicit path -- with
# 'supplemental_unpinned: true'. Two consequences are deliberate:
#
#   * The chain tries '.github/harden-runner/tykeal/allow_list.txt'
#     and then '.github/harden-runner/allow_list.txt'. A search-chain
#     miss is tolerated (soft); an explicit path that does not exist
#     is a hard error. That tolerance is what let the pull request
#     introducing this file run at all, since an unpinned supplemental
#     reads the default branch, where the file did not yet exist.
#   * The action permits an unpinned supplemental only when it lives
#     in the workflow's own org. Anyone who can merge here can already
#     edit the workflows, so following the default branch grants no
#     new trust -- and it means adding a host does not require bumping
#     a ref in every workflow. A cross-org list must always be pinned,
#     which is why the LF baseline is pinned to a commit.
#
# Because the supplemental is read from this repository's DEFAULT
# BRANCH over the network, and never from the checked-out tree, a pull
# request (including one from a fork) cannot widen its own egress
# allow-list by editing this file.
#
# File format (enforced by the action's sanitiser)
# ------------------------------------------------
#   * One 'host' or 'host:port' token per line; '#' starts a comment.
#   * '*.host' matches subdomains ONLY -- it does not include the bare
#     host -- and opens only the FIRST port listed for that wildcard.
#     Bare '*' is rejected.
#   * A file that parses to ZERO tokens is a hard error
#     ("config file is empty after parsing"), so this list must never
#     be reduced to comments alone. Delete the file and the
#     'supplemental_config' inputs together if it is ever emptied.
#   * Entries whose hostname does not resolve are dropped before
#     enforcement (invalid_records: filter), because harden-runner
#     reverts to no filtering at all if it cannot resolve an entry.
#
# Entries are sorted alphabetically. Every entry records why it is
# here, taken from observed egress in audit-mode runs of the jobs that
# consume this list (StepSecurity run data for the 'Type Check' and
# 'Zizmor' workflows), never from guesswork.
#
# Overlap with the LF baseline is intentional for these three. The
# action de-duplicates, so a repeated entry costs nothing, and the
# shared list is maintained for the whole LF estate rather than for
# this repository. Carrying this project's own toolchain hosts here
# means a future trim of the shared baseline cannot silently break
# 'uv sync' or the uv download.

# uv/Python wheel and sdist downloads during 'uv sync --locked'
# (Type Check). Observed: uv -> files.pythonhosted.org:443.
files.pythonhosted.org:443

# PyPI index metadata for 'uv sync --locked' (Type Check) and for the
# Python the zizmor action runs from (Zizmor).
# Observed: uv -> pypi.org:443, python3.14 -> pypi.org:443.
pypi.org:443

# uv binary download by astral-sh/setup-uv (Type Check).
# Observed: node -> releases.astral.sh:443.
releases.astral.sh:443
